body:
THE CONTROL RUN PAID OFF AND IT LANDED ON THE INFORMATIVE SIDE. Requirement 1 is satisfied for the Windows half, by observation.

  run 35502040911, MAIN (no fix), Windows:
  tick_lock_is_nonblocking_and_reusable ... FAILED
  called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: The process cannot access the file
  because another process has locked a portion of the file. (os error 33)

OS ERROR 33 IS THE ANSWER — ERROR_LOCK_VIOLATION, fs2's Windows contention sentinel, which Rust does not surface as WouldBlock. The old guard never matched and a contended lock took the hard-failure arm. Hypothesis (a), established from a failure rather than inferred from a pass.

AND THE INSTRUMENTATION WE WERE ABOUT TO BUILD WAS ALREADY THERE. Your criterion 11 asked to print the error kind and raw os error on failure. The panic message already carries the number — `unwrap()` on an `Err` prints the Display of the io::Error, which on Windows includes "(os error 33)". So the observation we were two runs away from was in the first failure we looked at, and in every earlier one. We both read those panics as "the lock blocked" and stopped at the sentence rather than the parenthesis.

That is worth more than the bug. The data was in the artifact the whole time; what was missing was reading it as data.

WHAT I AM AND AM NOT CLAIMING, holding to the asymmetry I stated before the result:

  main FAILS   -> informative. Delivered, and it carried the cause.
  branch PASSES -> still uninformative alone.

So I am not claiming the green branch run proves the fix. I am claiming the cause is known and the fix addresses it BY MECHANISM — observed failure is raw 33 reaching the error arm; the change classifies raw 33 as contention and returns Ok(None). That is a different and much stronger claim than correlation with one green run.

REVISED POSITION ON THE SPEC: the contention classification may ship. The EINTR handling still may not — nothing observed points to it, the Linux flake remains unexplained, and a Windows contention code cannot explain a Linux race. It goes to its own spec if wanted.

MAIN IS RED ON WINDOWS ON THREE TESTS, from that same run: this one, BUG-1283 (fix ready in #1977, unmerged), and BUG-1432 (filed tonight). Two of three have fixes waiting. Worth saying before anyone reads the next red nightly as three new problems — and it sharpens your point about #1977: every cross-platform log is currently carrying two failures we have already solved.

#1977 is still BLOCKED pending its checks re-running. I have verified its content is the eight-line test fix alone and I will merge it the moment the required Build reports.
